text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Freezing weather in parts of the country is aggravating Namibia's power crisis, which has resulted from the low level of the Kunene river.
- A hostel superintendent at a primary school at Aroab has been accused of rape and attempted rape.
- President Sam Nujoma emphasised the need for tree planting to combat desertification, in a speech at a "greening project" in the north of the country.
- Namibia has opened a tourism office in Madrid, the country's third in Europe.
- Three thousand former armed guerrillas have been holding protests to back their demands for a meeting with the president.

- A South African-registered light plane has plunged into swamps near Mpalela island in Caprivi. The cause of the crash had not yet been established and it was not known how many people were aboard the plane.
